set.notes: Magnesium oxide had about 4% fractional absorption in the human comparison by Firoz and Graber (PMID:11794633), and it performed no better than placebo in the longer Walker comparison (PMID:14596323). Its high elemental-magnesium percentage does not imply high absorption. It is also used as an osmotic laxative. Clinician recalibration 2026-06-02: bio_score is absorption/bioavailability only; natural/source and tolerability claims are not counted in bio_score. Magnesium bound to gluconic acid. Similar profile to lactate — gentle on the stomach with moderate absorption. Lower elemental magnesium content. Well-tolerated for daily supplementation without GI side effects. Evidence update 2026-04-25 (Batch 15): Magnesium audit — 11 PMIDs WebFetch-verified. CLASS FINDING: organic chelates (glycinate, malate, taurate, orotate, AAC, gluconate, aspartate, lactate, chloride) cluster F ~25-45% in humans with overlapping CIs; only robustly-replicated human ranking is citrate ≥ organic chelates > carbonate > oxide. THREONATE FINDING: BBB-crossing claim is RAT-ONLY (Slutsky 2010 PMID:20152124, Neuron). Liu 2016 + Zhang 2022 human cognitive RCTs have NO brain Mg PK. ACETYL-TAURATE: rodent-only (Ates 2019 mice, Uysal 2019 rats); no human PK. BROWN RICE CHELATE: re-confirmed 0 PubMed hits (Batch 11). Misattributions caught: Slutsky PMID 20152120→20152124; Walker 2003 did NOT test glycinate; Schwalfenberg 2017 muscle-cramps RCT does not exist; Coudray correction: PMID:16548135. Clinician recalibration 2026-06-02: bio_score is absorption/bioavailability only; natural/source and tolerability claims are not counted in bio_score.
